name: AionUi
vibe_summary: A polished cross-platform desktop 'cowork' app that wraps OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and 20+ other CLI agents into one 24/7 multi-agent workspace. Its vibe is a VS Code-style mission control for agent teams, with remote WebUI access and heavy i18n polish.
best_for: Users juggling multiple CLI coding agents who want one GUI
Teams wanting 24/7 agent automation with remote access
Non-CLI-fluent users who want a zero-setup agent front-end
avoid_if: You want a single tightly-integrated agent rather than a wrapper
You need strong sandboxing around agent shell execution
You prefer minimal resource usage over an Electron-style desktop app
openclaw_advantages: Unified GUI for 20+ CLI agents including OpenClaw itself
Multi-agent teaming and parallel session management
Remote WebUI access from phone/browser with session refresh
Polished UX: notifications, i18n in 13 locales, VS Code-style explorer
openclaw_disadvantages: It is a wrapper, not an agent — depends on OpenClaw/others for actual capability
Heavier Electron-style footprint vs OpenClaw's lean core
Less mature skills/plugin ecosystem than OpenClaw's registry
Shell access risk is inherited and amplified across multiple agents
confidence_summary: Strong evidence from README, release cadence, and detailed commit history that this is an actively maintained OpenClaw-compatible cowork app. Reddit sentiment is noisy (many irrelevant 'Aion' MMORPG matches), so community sentiment confidence is moderate.

overview_markdown:
AionUi is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) desktop 'cowork' application that acts as a unified front-end for OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and 20+ other CLI agents. Rather than being an agent itself, it provides a VS Code-style workspace — file explorer, SCM/changes panel, conversation sidebar — where multiple agents can run in parallel, be customized, and be teamed up for 24/7 automation. It ships cross-platform builds for macOS, Windows, and Linux, supports any API key, and offers a remote WebUI so agents can be monitored from a phone browser.

Architecturally it is a TypeScript/Electron-style app backed by an 'aioncore' service, with recent engineering focused on robustness: tab-scoped explorer refresh with repository re-discovery, websocket reconnect backoff fixes, silent session refresh on 401s for the remote WebUI, and richer notification states that distinguish 'waiting for user confirmation' from active generation. Security posture is middling — it orchestrates agents with shell access and mentions permission/confirmation flows, but there is no evidence of strong sandboxing.

Compared to OpenClaw itself, AionUi is complementary rather than competitive: OpenClaw is one of the agents it hosts. Its differentiators are the multi-agent GUI, team orchestration, remote access, and polish (13 locales, desktop notifications), while OpenClaw remains stronger as a standalone assistant with a large skills ecosystem.
